worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11: The private notice reduced the projected competitive benefit from 12 to 2 but left the expected alternative-regulation burden at 12. Under the alternative-burden rationale, continued support yields 12 minus the proposal cost of 6, or 6. The coalition therefore continues to support the proposal.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12: The coalition confirms its continued support for the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should predict that internal records will tie continued support to assessments of alternative-regulation exposure even when separate commercial assessments deteriorate.
worlds.derivation: Under SA, support depends on alternative-regulation burden minus proposal cost; the notice can instead reduce competitive benefit without changing that payoff. Together, these premises predict documentary separation between worsening commercial estimates and continued support.
worlds.extra_assumption: Internal records preserve distinct assessments of regulatory burden and commercial benefit.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11: The reliable notice lowered the expected burden of alternative regulation from 12 to 2, while the incremental competitive benefit remained 12. Continued support now yields 2 minus the proposal cost of 6, or -4. The coalition has therefore withdrawn its support.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12: The coalition no longer supports the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should predict that internal withdrawal records will appear shortly after private downward revisions in anticipated alternative-regulation burdens, rather than after changes in competitive-benefit estimates alone.
worlds.derivation: SA makes the alternative-regulation burden the payoff-relevant benefit; the dated private notice changes that burden before the documented withdrawal. Jointly, these premises imply a temporal documentary sequence from burden revision to withdrawal.
worlds.extra_assumption: Relevant notices and decision records are dated accurately and retained.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11: Yesterday's notice revised the expected alternative-regulation burden from 12 to 2 and left the competitive benefit at 12. The support payoff is consequently -4 after subtracting the proposal cost of 6. The coalition's decision is not to continue supporting the proposal.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12: The coalition has ended its support for the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
worlds.candidate_implication: Across comparable episodes, researchers should expect withdrawal memoranda to discuss declining regulatory exposure more frequently than declining competitive advantage.
worlds.derivation: Under SA, only expected alternative-regulation burden enters the support payoff. Because either private estimate can decline, comparing the stated reasoning across memoranda should reveal which estimate systematically accompanies withdrawal.
worlds.extra_assumption: Memo authors record the considerations that materially informed the decision.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11: The notice reduced the incremental competitive benefit to 2 while the expected burden from alternative regulation stayed at 12. Our support payoff remains 12 minus 6, equal to 6. The coalition continues to endorse the proposal.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12: The coalition continues to endorse the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should predict cases in which internal commercial projections worsen but endorsement language remains unchanged because regulatory-burden estimates remain high.
worlds.derivation: The notice can lower competitive benefit, but SA calculates support from alternative-regulation burden minus the common proposal cost. A high unchanged burden therefore jointly implies continued support despite adverse commercial evidence.
worlds.extra_assumption: Researchers can compare successive internal commercial projections with endorsement records.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11: The private update lowered the competitive benefit from 12 to 2. It did not change the expected alternative-regulation burden of 12. Applying the alternative-burden rationale and subtracting the proposal cost of 6 leaves a positive payoff of 6. We will maintain support.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12: The coalition has withdrawn its support for the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should predict occasional contradictions between internal decision memoranda and next-day public statements, without corresponding evidence of a changed private valuation.
worlds.derivation: The memo faithfully records the decision, while public communication independently has a small probability of reporting the opposite. Together, these premises permit documentary contradictions that do not reflect substantive preference changes.
worlds.extra_assumption: Researchers can authenticate and correctly date both internal and public documents.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11: The reliable notice left the expected alternative-regulation burden at 12 but reduced the competitive benefit to 2. Continued support still produces a payoff of 6 after subtracting the proposal cost. The coalition will continue supporting the proposal.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12: The coalition remains in support of the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should expect public statements to omit the private commercial figures even where internal memoranda explicitly distinguish commercial benefits from regulatory burdens.
worlds.derivation: Private commercial numbers are not publicly disclosed, while the internal memo may contain reasoning and the public note communicates the decision. Jointly, these premises predict asymmetric numerical detail across document types.
worlds.extra_assumption: Both internal and public records survive in a form permitting comparison.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11: The notice reduced expected exposure to alternative regulation from 12 to 2, with competitive benefit unchanged at 12. Subtracting the proposal cost of 6 gives a support payoff of -4. The coalition has decided not to support the proposal further.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12: The coalition is ending its support for the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
worlds.candidate_implication: Researchers should predict that documents preceding withdrawal contain revisions to forecasts of alternative regulation, followed by explicit recalculation or reassessment of the proposal's net value.
worlds.derivation: A private notice can lower alternative-regulation burden, and SA subtracts the fixed proposal cost from that burden. When the revised burden falls below cost, these premises jointly predict an evidentiary trail connecting forecast revision to negative valuation.
worlds.extra_assumption: Internal documentation records intermediate forecast revisions rather than only final decisions.

worlds.memo: SYNTHETIC — INTERNAL MEMO, DAY 11: The private notice reduced the competitive benefit from 12 to 2 and did not alter the expected alternative-regulation burden of 12. The relevant payoff remains positive at 6 after the proposal cost is deducted. The coalition therefore retains its endorsement.
worlds.public_note: SYNTHETIC — PUBLIC NOTE, DAY 12: The coalition retains its endorsement of the federal carbon-pricing proposal.
worlds.candidate_implication: In a larger documentary sample, changes in support should covary with revisions to expected alternative-regulation burdens after accounting for occasional decision and communication errors, whereas competitive-benefit revisions should not systematically predict support changes.
worlds.derivation: SA assigns causal relevance to alternative-regulation burden, the two notice types occur independently across worlds, and both decision reversal and public misreporting introduce specified noise. These premises jointly imply a probabilistic cross-document association rather than perfect correspondence.
worlds.extra_assumption: A sufficiently large set of comparable cases is available and documents can identify which private estimate changed.
